# Muse Code for DeepSeek Harness
Muse Code subscription integration for DeepSeek Harness

DeepSeek Harness (DSH) ships Meta's Muse Code subscription as the pi-ai `meta`
provider with its dev

ice-code sign-in flow. This bundle connects that
provider to the surfaces you work in: it declares t

he route so the provider
appears under **Settings → Models** and in the model picker, and it adds th

e
**Muse Code OAuth** settings page and the `/muse-login` command that run the
shipped sign-in. No h
and-copied key, no duplicated provider code.

Since 2026-10-29 Meta rejects subscription requests whose client tool
declarations collide with Muse

Code's builtin tool names, so the bundle ships
a loopback wire adapter that aliases exactly those n

ames toward `api.meta.ai`
and restores them in the answer. The behavior is pinned in
ADAPTER_CONTRAC

toward `api.meta.ai`
and restores them in the answer. The behavior is pinned in
ADAPTER_CONTRACT.md.

> **Unofficial and experimental.** This plugin uses a Muse Code subscription
> credential from DeepS

eek Harness. Meta's terms limit that credential to Muse
> Code, so this use may not be supported and

Meta may suspend or revoke accounts
> or credentials. Use it at your own risk. Read DISCLAIMER.md

No manual profile edit is required. Restart DSH after installing or upgrading.
## Quick start

1. Install the bundle and restart DSH.
2. Open **Settings → Muse Code OAuth** and press **Sign in wi

th Meta**. The
Host runs DSH's device-code flow, opens the verification page, and shows the
code.
3.

Confirm the code on Meta's page; the page switches to **Signed in** and DSH
stores the credential.
4. Pick a Muse model in the model picker, for example `muse-spark-1.3`.

If the Settings page cannot reach the Host, run `/muse-login` in a chat instead;
it runs the same fl

ow (how the sign-in fits together). The
page states, actions, and provider-row migration are documen

ted in
docs/settings-page.md.
## Features

- Declares the shipped `meta` provider route as `muse-code-oauth` for
Settings → Models and the mode

l picker.
- Syncs the account's live chat catalog into the route, so new chat models
appear without

a DSH catalog update. A model list you edited is never
overwritten.
- Adds a **Muse Code OAuth** set

tings page with live status, device code, and
Meta page link, plus the `/muse-login` chat command. B

oth start DSH's
device-code flow.
- Paints the native credential dot on the provider row and re-mint

s the key
before Meta's ~24 h expiry.
- Routes inference through a loopback adapter that aliases col

liding tool
names and normalizes parameters (`MUSE_CODE_ADAPTER=off` keeps the proxy,
drops the resh

aping).
- Leaves credential handling to DSH: the shipped flow stores the sign-in and
the plugin keep
s the route's reference copy fresh.
## Requirements

- DeepSeek Harness `0.2.1-rc.3` or newer, with the pi-ai `meta` provider.
- Node.js 20 or newer on t

he DSH host; CI runs Node.js 20, 22, and 24.
- A Meta account with an active Muse Code subscription.
- No separate service, CLI, or key file.
## Configuration
| Setting | Purpose | Default |
| `muse-code-oauth` provider route | The shipped `meta` route, declared by the bundle; shown under S

ettings → Models and in the model picker. | declared on first boot |
| **Muse Code OAuth** page | St

arts the device-code flow and follows the status until **Signed in**. | available after install |
|

`/muse-login` | The same sign-in from a chat or CLI surface. | available after install |
| Live mode
l catalog | Account chat models, written into the route when it has no list. | synced after sign-in

|
| `META_API_KEY` | Optional pay-as-you-go key accepted instead of the sign-in. | unset |
| `MUSE_C

ODE_ADAPTER` | `off` keeps the local proxy but disables the reshaping. | unset |
| Model | Any model
the route serves. | `muse-spark-1.3` |

The route reads the mirrored key through `MUSE_CODE_SUB_TOKEN`. Caching behaves
like any other pi-ai
route (measured behavior).

Installs upgraded from 0.3.x stored **Muse Code (Meta subscription)** as the
route label. 0.4.0 rena

mes that legacy label to `muse-code-oauth` on the next
boot and keeps a display name edited by hand.
## Privacy and security

- The bundle calls `GET /v1/models` on `api.meta.ai` to sync the catalog and
`/muse-code/key` to ref

resh the key. DSH owns the sign-in and the credential
store; verification happens on `https://auth.m

eta.com`.
- The local sign-in routes and the wire adapter listen on loopback only and
transmit no cr

edential. The adapter forwards `Authorization` unchanged and
never reads, stores, or logs credential

s or bodies.
- To remove access, remove the bundle and the declared provider, and delete
the `llm-pi
-ai/meta` record while DSH is stopped.

See SECURITY.md for vulnerability reporting,
AUTH_CONTRACT.md for the pinned login contract, and
ADA
PTER_CONTRACT.md for the inference wire rules.
## Troubleshooting
### The `muse-code-oauth` row is missing from Settings → Models

The bundle was not loaded by the active profile, or the profile lacks the
`llm-pi-ai` adapter. Re-ru

n the install command for the same profile, restart
DSH, and check for `did not activate` warnings.

Without the pi-ai Meta
provider, update DSH.
### The sign-in page cannot reach the Host

Some Desktop and non-loopback deployments cannot reach the local Web route, and
the Host opens the b

rowser on a best-effort basis. Open the Meta page from the
shown link, enter the code, and if the Mu

se Code OAuth page never flips to
**Signed in**, run `/muse-login` in a chat instead; it waits for M

eta's
confirmation itself.
### Meta rejects subscription requests from this client

A 403 mentioning `client_attestation_denied` should no longer happen for
colliding tool names while

the adapter runs. If it does, the adapter could not
bind a loopback port, `MUSE_CODE_ADAPTER=off` is

set, or Meta changed the gate.
Signing in again does not change it; the alternatives are Muse Code

itself or
a pay-as-you-go key.
